60120970.s: Aisha Al Rajhi Mosque in Makkah is a large mosque owned by the Sulaiman bin Abdulaziz Al Rajhi Endowment Company, part of Sulaiman Al Rajhi Holding Endowments. It was opened on 22 Shaaban 1434 AH in the presence of the Emir of Makkah Region, Prince Khalid Al-Faisal.
60120970.b:

60120806.t: Exhibition Of The Two Holy Mosques Architecture
60120806.s: The Two Holy Mosques Museum is one of the museums of Makkah Region and is run by the General Presidency for the Affairs of the Grand Mosque and the Prophet's Mosque. Established in 1999, it is an exhibition on the Two Holy Mosques and the development of their architecture through the ages. It has seven halls with two models of the Two Holy Mosques and a range of items including manuscripts, inscriptions, precious artefacts, architectural models and rare photographs.

60120763.s: Makkah Museum (Al Zahir Palace Museum) is one of the museums of Makkah Region. Work began on building the palace in 1365 AH (1946 AD) by order of King Abdulaziz and took seven years, finishing in 1372 AH (1952 AD). It was used for a time as a guest palace and in 1378 AH was given to the Ministry of Education of the time, which turned it into the home of Al Zahir Intermediate School and converted its rooms and halls into classrooms. It was used this way until 1398 AH, when the building was handed to the Antiquities and Museums Agency, which carried out a comprehensive restoration and returned it to its original architectural condition.

60120635.s: Cave Thawr lies on the northern side of Mount Thawr, south of Makkah, about four kilometres south of the Grand Mosque (Masjid al-Haram). It is the cave in which the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq took refuge on their way to Madinah during the Hijrah. It stands 760 metres above sea level.

60120633.s: Masjid Al-Tan'im, also known as Masjid Aisha, is one of the mosques of Makkah. It lies in the western part of Makkah, 7 km from the Grand Mosque, and is a point from which the people of Makkah enter the state of ihram for Hajj and Umrah. It is famous because it was built on the spot where the Mother of the Believers, Aisha bint Abi Bakr, entered ihram for Umrah during the Farewell Pilgrimage in the year 9 AH.

60120631.s: Jinn Mosque, formerly called the Guards' Mosque, is a historic mosque in Makkah, in the Al Ghazzah district near the Grand Mosque (Masjid al-Haram). It was so named because the night watchmen would gather there at night. It is said to mark the place that the Prophet (peace be upon him) marked out for Ibn Masud on the night the jinn listened to him, and where the jinn pledged allegiance to the Prophet (peace be upon him).

60120607.s: Al Sakkaf Palace is a historic palace in Makkah, in western Saudi Arabia. It was a seat of state and a centre of government under King Abdulaziz and King Saud bin Abdulaziz. One of Makkah's older buildings, it has an Islamic architectural character, with many Islamic artistic elements and decorations.

60120601.s: The Grand Mosque (Masjid al-Haram) is the greatest mosque in Islam and stands in the heart of the city of Makkah in western Saudi Arabia. At its centre is the Kaaba, which according to Islamic belief is the first house established for people to worship God in, and the greatest and holiest spot on earth for Muslims. It is the direction Muslims face in prayer and the place they go on pilgrimage. It is called Masjid al-Haram because fighting there is forbidden, from the time the Prophet Muhammad entered Makkah in triumph. Muslims believe that prayer in it is worth one hundred thousand prayers.

60075214.t: Scitech - Sultan bin Abdulaziz Science and Technology Center
60075214.s: Sultan bin Abdulaziz Science and Technology Center (Scitech) is one of the projects of the Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz Al Saud Charitable Foundation. The idea for the center arose in 2000, when Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz (may God have mercy on him) ordered a science center modelled on the world's most modern science centers, to serve students, researchers in science and technology, and all groups of society.
60075214.b:
Sultan bin Abdulaziz Science and Technology Center (Scitech) is one of the projects of the Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz Al Saud Charitable Foundation. The idea for the center arose in 2000, when Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz (may God have mercy on him) ordered a science center modelled on the world's most modern science centers, to serve students, researchers in science and technology, and all groups of society.

Because Prince Sultan wanted the center to be given to a body concerned with science and technology, he ordered it donated to King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals in 2006, making it one of the active centers serving and raising awareness in the community. In 2022 the center moved to the Eastern Province Development Authority to carry on the scientific, social and cultural renaissance project.

The center is on the Khobar Corniche, on a site of 21,700 square metres, with a building area of 14,100 square metres, designed and built on the model of the world's most modern centers. It includes four main exhibition halls covering a range of scientific and cultural fields, an IMAX science dome, an astronomical observatory, a conference hall (theatre), multi-purpose exhibition halls, and administrative facilities and services.

The center's main aim is to educate members of the community, especially young people, through an engaging, interactive approach based on learning through entertainment and learning through experience and observation.

60075182.t: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture - Ithra
60075182.s: The King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture, or Ithra, is a cultural center owned by Saudi Aramco. It stands on the same site in Dhahran where Bir Al-Khair (the Well of Goodness), the Kingdom's first oil well, was discovered. Its design takes the form of a group of stacked stones that hold a modern library, an innovation center, an Idea Lab for children that is the first museum of its kind for children in the Arab world, a natural history museum, art halls and an archive center. The Knowledge Tower rises in the middle, offering educational programs for pioneers of all ages.
60075182.b: The King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture, or Ithra, is a cultural center owned by Saudi Aramco. The Knowledge Tower rises in the middle, offering educational programs for pioneers of all ages. In 2018 it was chosen by the American magazine Time as one of the 100 greatest places in the world.

60075179.s: "The Energy Exhibit presents achievements of the past and present, and the challenges of the future."
60075179.b:
"The Energy Exhibit presents achievements of the past and present, and the challenges of the future."

The Energy Exhibit, formerly the Saudi Aramco Oil Exhibit, draws visitors in with modern technology and varied media. It centres on oil, science, energy and technology, and takes visitors on a journey from the beginnings of petroleum and the formation of rocks underground, through drilling in the desert, to refineries and the Kingdom's alternative energy solutions.
